---
title: "Method Formulation"
---

## Implicit Variational Family

Let \(p(z)\) denote the unnormalized target density. We use an implicit variational sampler

\[
z = g_\theta(\epsilon, \eta), \qquad
\epsilon \sim p_\epsilon,\quad \eta \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I),
\]

which induces a marginal variational distribution \(q_\theta\) over \(z\). The density \(q_\theta(z)\) may be unavailable or inconvenient, but drawing samples from \(q_\theta\) is cheap and differentiable with respect to \(\theta\).

## MCMC Pushforward

Let \(T\) be a Markov transition kernel with invariant distribution \(p\). For a current distribution \(q\), the pushforward \(T_\# q\) is the distribution obtained by first drawing \(z \sim q\), then drawing \(z' \sim T(\cdot \mid z)\). Repeating the transition \(K\) times gives

\[
z' \sim T_\#^K q_\theta .
\]

If the transition kernel mixes toward \(p\), then \(T_\#^K q_\theta\) can be viewed as an MCMC-improved version of \(q_\theta\).

## Distillation Objective

The training objective is to make the implicit sampler match its own MCMC-improved distribution:

\[
\min_\theta D\!\left(q_\theta,\; T_\#^K q_\theta\right),
\]

where \(D\) is a sample-based discrepancy between distributions. In the current method, \(D\) is Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD).

For a minibatch \(z_i = g_\theta(\epsilon_i,\eta_i)\), run \(K\) MCMC steps from detached particles to obtain \(\tilde z_i\). The loss is

\[
\mathcal{L}(\theta)
=
\widehat{\operatorname{MMD}}^2
\left(
\{z_i\}_{i=1}^n,\,
\{\operatorname{sg}(\tilde z_i)\}_{i=1}^n
\right),
\]

where \(\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)\) is stop-gradient. Gradients flow through the variational samples \(z_i\), but not through the MCMC transition.

## MMD Estimator

With kernel \(k\), the biased V-statistic estimator is

\[
\widehat{\operatorname{MMD}}^2
=
\frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i,j} k(z_i,z_j)
+ \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i,j} k(\tilde z_i,\tilde z_j)
- \frac{2}{n^2}\sum_{i,j} k(z_i,\tilde z_j).
\]

The first term keeps the variational particles spread out, while the cross term pulls them toward MCMC-improved particles. The second term is useful for the value of the discrepancy, but it is detached from the optimization path.

## Fixed-Point Intuition

If \(q_\theta = p\), then applying an invariant transition leaves the distribution unchanged:

\[
T_\# p = p.
\]

Thus \(q_\theta=p\) is a distributional fixed point of the objective. Conversely, when \(q_\theta\) is not close to \(p\), a short MCMC chain usually moves samples toward regions preferred by the target. Distillation trains the sampler to reproduce that movement directly.

This is not a claim that every finite neural sampler and every short transition yields a formal contraction. The useful intuition is gentler: the MCMC kernel supplies local target-directed corrections, and the variational sampler amortizes those corrections across training.
